title: SQL Introduction
summary: SQL asks questions about information in tables. Read rows and columns, and try a tiny table of books.
introduction: A class list has rows and columns. A database can store information in tables like that list. SQL is a language for asking the database questions. A question written in SQL is called a query. You can try SQL on this site without making an account or setting up a server.
learningObjectives: Explain a table, a row and a column
Run a small query that finds one book

blocks.text: A table is an organised list

rows: Information arranged in rows and columns.
One item, such as one book.
One kind of fact, such as a book title.
A question or instruction written in SQL.

blocks.text: `SELECT` asks for an answer. `AS total` names the answer column `total`. A semicolon ends the instruction.
This example makes a tiny list inside the query. `WITH` gives the list a name for this query only. You can run the example more than once.

blocks.title: Two books

blocks.content:
title | pages
Garden Days | 40
Moon Trip | 60

items: `books` is the table name for this query.
`title` and `pages` are the two column names.
Each pair inside `VALUES` is one row.
`FROM books` tells SQL which table to read.

blocks.title: Find a book with more than 50 pages

blocks.text: `WHERE` gives a rule for the rows we want. `pages > 50` means "more than 50 pages." Only Moon Trip fits. We asked for `title`, so the answer shows that column.

blocks.title: Watch out
blocks.text: SQL text uses single quotes, like `'Moon Trip'`. Numbers such as 60 do not need quotes. SQL tools have small differences. The Run button here uses SQLite.

blocks.title: Your turn
blocks.text: Change `50` to `30` in the last example. Guess which books will appear, then run it. Can you choose a number that gives no rows?

seo.title: SQL Introduction – Tables, Queries and Dialects
seo.description: Learn what SQL is, how relational databases organise data in tables, and run your first SELECT statements in a browser-based SQLite playground.
